Software/reference target part = onsemi (ex-Fairchild) FUSB302B, orderable variant FUSB302BMPX (I2C slave addr 0100010b = 0x22, matching the DT node). Note: the ET7301B's own datasheet was NOT sourced (web-search budget exhausted), so the dims/price below are for the onsemi FUSB302BMPX reference part, not proven to be the exact silicon on the board.

result.board: microduck-banana-contact-pcb — the "banana" battery-contact board in the trunk. It is the passive interface between the removable NP-F550 2S Li-ion pack and the RPi Robot HAT: battery blade contacts on one face, two power conductors (VBAT/BAT+ and GND/BAT-) out to the HAT. It is known only indirectly: the printed part microduck-banana-pcb-locker (a 54 x 1.5 x 6.6 mm retaining bar, two M2 Ø2.17 holes in Ø4 eyes, 12 mm centre notch, two key tabs) bolts to the power_support's two Ø3.9 pins and clamps this PCB into the power_support cradle (54.5 x 17.0 x 83.5 mm). Power path is confirmed by the netlist and firmware: battery -> banana contact PCB -> HAT -> Radxa Zero 3W; firmware has no fuel gauge and no ADC, so the board does no sensing.

result.summary:
Microduck electronics verification for manufacturing release. Roster: 22 distinct per-robot electronics line items. Only 2 are release-grade VERIFIED (Dynamixel XL330-M288-T servo x15, identity + live sourced price + ROBOTIS-quoted dims; and Radxa Zero 3W host, identity + official-drawing L/W dims 65x30 mm + live ALLNET price). 10 are PARTIAL: identity is firm (mostly from Pollen's own device-tree / runtime source or a priced representative part) but the exact production part, a key value, or a captured pinout/footprint is still open (X3P cables, NP-F550 pack, IMX219 camera+M12 lens, VL53L5CX/L8CX ToF, TLV320AIC3104 codec, dormant BMI088, LSM6DSV16X, and the included gamepad/USB-C cable). 10 are CANNOT DETERMINE: part identity or price fundamentally unknown (74LVC1G125 transceiver and D30V30F5 buck are OUR reconstructions of unpublished HAT parts; speaker, mic, NFC reader+2 antennas, REC LED, MIPI ribbon; and the three custom boards P1 Robot HAT / P2 imu_to_dxl v2 / P3 banana battery-contact PCB, none of which Pollen has published).

COST @ qty1: sourced electronics lines sum to a FLOOR of $465.64 (15 servos @ $23.90 intl = $358.50 [$412.35 at ROBOTIS-US $27.49, floor -> $519.49]; 2x X3P cable 10-packs $31.00; NP-F550 + charger share $24.95; IMX219 B0183 camera incl. lens $23.99; VL53L8CX ToF breakout $24.95; TLV320AIC3104 codec $2.25). This is a floor, not the BOM: it EXCLUDES the Radxa host price (the cited 1GB/32GB config is not a catalog SKU -> CANNOT DETERMINE, band $23-$50), both custom board+assembly quotes (P1/P2), the banana PCB, speaker, mic, NFC, REC LED, MIPI ribbon, and the two reconstruction-only ICs that would fold into the HAT quote. So true per-robot electronics cost is materially above $465.

COST @ qty100: CANNOT DETERMINE (null). The servo line is 77% of the sourced subtotal and NO distributor publishes a qty-100 tier for XL330 (needs a ROBOTIS OEM/bulk quote); only the codec ($1.389@100+) and ToF breakout ($19.43@100+) have volume pricing, and the Radxa/camera/battery/cables have none. Without the dominant servo volume price the qty-100 total cannot be summed honestly.

House rule held throughout: every price carries a distributor URL; every gap is reported CANNOT DETERMINE with null, never guessed. Sources: docs/BOM.md, out/release/bom.csv, docs/ELECTRONICS-AND-SOFTWARE.md, electronics/netlist.json.
